items.headline: Judge tosses Trump's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal
items.summary: A federal judge dismissed President Trump's defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a story about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. The ruling comes days before Tuesday's midterm elections.

items.headline: Justice Department moves to isolate Alaska Senate ballots
items.summary: The Justice Department is seeking to set aside some Alaska ballots as a criminal probe examines claims that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate in the toss-up Senate race. The request comes days before Tuesday's election.

items.headline: Virginia and D.C. sue to stop Trump's triumphal arch
items.summary: Virginia and the District of Columbia sued to block construction of President Trump's planned arch in Washington, joining existing legal challenges. A federal judge ordered both sides to agree on a briefing schedule for a restraining order request.

items.headline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000
items.summary: Congolese health ministry figures show 5,026 deaths among 10,351 people infected, a fatality rate near 50 percent. Fears are growing that the outbreak could spread across the continent.

items.headline: Oleshky evacuees reach Ukrainian-held territory
items.summary: Civilians evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrived in Ukraine after traveling through Russia and Belarus. The evacuation took place under a localized ceasefire.

items.headline: Youth-led cost-of-living protests sweep France
items.summary: About 320,000 people marched across France over rising living costs as youth-led protests spread in Europe. France's interior minister warned of a very high risk of disorder.

items.headline: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta talks without consensus
items.summary: Foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta did not agree on a joint communique on key issues. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is to release a chairman's statement summarizing the talks instead.

items.headline: China's party leaders stress discipline before Xi's expected fourth term
items.summary: A Chinese Communist Party Central Committee meeting this week focused on discipline and anti-corruption. Xi Jinping is widely expected to seek a fourth term next year.

items.headline: Americans lost nearly $18 billion to cyberscams, probe finds
items.summary: A congressional investigation identified gaps in federal efforts to help Americans recover money lost to online scams. Losses to cyberscams reached nearly $18 billion last year.

items.headline: Midterm results may take days, and that's normal
items.summary: A fact check explains that counting ballots after Tuesday's midterm elections can take days, as in past cycles. It also addresses false claims that late-counted ballots signal fraud.

digest.overview:
A federal judge in Miami dismissed President Trump's defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over its Epstein story, finding no proof of actual malice. The Justice Department asked a court to segregate Alaska ballots ranking independent Senate candidate Daniel J. Sullivan, while the state moved to dismiss the suit and the FBI contacted Sullivan's donors. Early voting topped 49.5 million ballots by Friday evening, including more than 6.3 million in Texas. Trump held six telerallies Saturday ahead of in-person stops in Kansas and Iowa. Virginia and the District of Columbia sued to block Trump's planned triumphal arch. Pope Leo became the first pontiff to vote in a U.S. general election. A shooting at a Halloween store in Fairfield, California, killed one and injured six.

Abroad, Iran said it is discussing a two-day plan with Qatari mediators to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, even as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered an unrestricted response to any threat. Oleshky evacuees reached Ukraine via Russia and Belarus, and a Russian drone strike in Dnipro killed at least 14. Thousands rallied in Tel Aviv for a Jewish-Arab coalition to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu. U.S., South Korean and Japanese foreign ministers reaffirmed North Korea's complete denuclearization at the G20 in Atlanta, which ended without a joint communique, and Pyongyang said sanctions cannot change its nuclear status. China's Communist Party Central Committee met on discipline ahead of Xi Jinping's expected fourth-term bid. About 320,000 people protested living costs in France, and youth protests turned violent in Frankfurt. Congo's Ebola deaths passed 5,000.

home.overview:
Victor Wembanyama poured in a season-high 43 points with six blocks as San Antonio beat Minnesota 121–111, Jabari Smith Jr. scored 30 in Houston's 119–98 win over short-handed Oklahoma City, and Tyrese Maxey's 38 lifted Philadelphia to 6–1 without LeBron James and Joel Embiid. Memphis stayed perfect at 6–0. NFL Week 8 is loaded today: Lamar Jackson returns at Buffalo, Kansas City visits Denver with the AFC West at stake, Cleveland and Pittsburgh meet tied atop the AFC North, and Eagles–Commanders closes the night. Washington lost Daron Payne for the season, and the Colts are fielding interest in Jonathan Taylor.

Brighton won 1–0 at Manchester City for City's second straight league loss, and Chelsea beat Man United 2–0 as Cole Palmer scored his 50th Premier League goal. Liverpool host Arsenal today. Bayern and Dortmund drew 2–2 in Der Klassiker after Harry Kane hit the crossbar from the spot, and Barcelona thrashed Alavés 6–1 to stay two points clear of Atlético. In K League 1, Incheon stunned champions FC Seoul 1–0 with a stoppage-time winner. In the KBO, Samsung beat Kia 6–1 in Game 5 behind Ariel Jurado to set up a Korean Series against KT Wiz from Tuesday.

brief: Samsung beat Kia 6–1 in Game 5 in Daegu on Sunday to win the second round 3–2 before a sellout crowd of 23,550.
Ariel Jurado allowed one run over seven innings and was named series MVP.
Kim Ji-chan had three hits and three RBIs, including a sixth-inning triple, after Samsung scored four runs in the first two innings.
Samsung face regular-season champion KT Wiz in the best-of-seven Korean Series, starting Tuesday at 6:30 p.m. in Suwon; KT have not played since Oct. 12.
